items.title: Correlating the Seven with the Forty (Part 2), and How Each Attention Conditions the Next

items.zh: 自然運轉作意，加行究竟及此果二作意攝。思擇作意，了相所攝。內攝作意，勝解所攝。淨障作意，遠離、攝樂、觀察、加行究竟作意所攝。依止成辦所行清淨作意，唯加行究竟果作意所攝。
items.en: The spontaneous-running attention is subsumed by the consummation-of-means attention and its fruit. The discernment attention is subsumed by knowing-marks; the inward-gathering attention by resolute-conviction. The obstruction-purifying attention is subsumed by seclusion, delight-in-gathering, investigation, and consummation-of-means; the purity-of-conduct-accomplished-in-reliance attention is subsumed only by the fruit-of-consummation attention.

items.zh: 他所建立、內增上取作意，一切作意所攝。廣大作意皆所不攝。初遍行作意，加行究竟果攝；第二，一切所攝。又了相作意若他所建立作意攝者，以聞他音、及內如理作意定為其緣。若內增上取作意攝者，唯先資糧以為其緣。所餘作意，前前後後傳為其緣。
items.en: The established-by-others and inner-ascendancy attentions are subsumed by all [seven]; the vast attention is subsumed by none; the first all-pervading attention is subsumed by the fruit-of-consummation, the second by all. Moreover, the knowing-marks attention, where subsumed under the established-by-others attention, definitely has as its condition both the hearing of another's voice and inner sound attention; where subsumed under the inner-ascendancy attention, it has only the prior [accumulated] provisions as its condition. As for the remaining attentions, each earlier one serves as the condition for each later one in turn.

items.title: The Object of Meditation: Its Four Marks

items.zh: 復次，云何所緣差別？謂相差別。何等為相？略有四種。一、所緣相，二、因緣相，三、應遠離相，四、應修習相。所緣相者，謂所知事分別體相。因緣相者，謂定資糧。應遠離相復有四種。謂沈相、掉相、亂相、著相。應修習相當知對治此四種相。
items.en: Furthermore, what are the distinctions of object? They are distinctions of mark. What are the marks? In brief, four: first, the object-mark; second, the causal mark; third, the mark to be avoided; fourth, the mark to be cultivated. The object-mark is the discriminated substance-mark of the known thing. The causal mark is the provisions for concentration. The mark to be avoided is again fourfold: the marks of dullness, agitation, scatter, and attachment. The mark to be cultivated should be known as the antidote to these four marks.

items.title: Two Obstacles Anatomized: Dullness and Agitation

items.zh: 何等沈相？謂不守根門、食不知量、初夜後夜不常覺寤勤修觀行、不正知住，是癡行性，耽著睡眠、無巧便慧、惡作俱行欲勤心觀。不曾修習正奢摩他，於奢摩他未為純善，一向思惟奢摩他相。其心惛闇，於勝境界不樂攀緣。
items.en: What is the mark of dullness? Not guarding the sense-doors, not knowing the measure in food, not constantly practising wakeful contemplation in the first and last watches, not dwelling with clear comprehension — this is the deluded temperament. [With it:] clinging to sleep, lacking skilful wisdom, and the four bases of spiritual power — aspiration, effort, mind, and investigation — accompanied by remorse. Never having cultivated right calm, not yet adept at calm, one-sidedly dwelling on the mark of calm alone: the mind grows murky and takes no delight in engaging the excellent object.

items.zh: 何等掉相？謂不守根門等四，如前廣說，是貪行性。樂不寂靜、無厭離心、無巧便慧、太舉俱行，如前欲等。不曾修舉，於舉未善，唯一向修。由於種種隨順掉法親里尋等動亂其心。
items.en: What is the mark of agitation? The same four failures — not guarding the sense-doors and so on, as explained above — this is the greedy temperament. [With it:] delighting in non-quietude, lacking a mind of disenchantment, lacking skilful wisdom, and an over-elevation accompanying [those same four bases of power]. Never having cultivated [balanced] uplift, not yet adept at uplift, one-sidedly cultivating it alone. Through all the various agitation-prone thoughts — of loved ones and the rest — the mind is stirred and disturbed.

items.title: Two More Obstacles: Scatter and Attachment — and What to Cultivate Against All Four

items.zh: 何等亂相？謂不守根門等四，如前應知、是鈍根性，多求、多務、多諸事業、尋思行性，無巧便慧、無厭離心、不修遠離。於勝境界不樂攀緣，親近憒鬧，方便間缺、不審了知亂不亂相。
items.en: What is the mark of scatter? The same four failures, as known above. This is the dull-facultied temperament — much seeking, much busyness, many undertakings, the discursive temperament. Lacking skilful wisdom, lacking a mind of disenchantment, not cultivating seclusion; taking no delight in engaging the excellent object, keeping close to clamour, deficient in method, and not carefully discerning the mark of scatter from the mark of non-scatter.

items.zh: 何等著相？謂不守根門等四，如前應知。是鈍根性，是愛行性，多煩惱性。不如理思，不見過患，又於增上無出離見。對治如是應遠離相，隨其所應，當知即是應修習相。
items.en: What is the mark of attachment? The same four failures, as known above. This is the dull-facultied temperament, the craving temperament, the much-afflicted temperament. Not thinking soundly, not seeing the faults [of the world], and having no vision of release beyond the fortunate rebirths. The antidote to these marks-to-be-avoided, each as fits, should be known to be precisely the mark-to-be-cultivated.

items.title: The Thirty-Two Marks, and the First: Reading One's Own Mind

items.zh: 復有三十二相。謂自心相、外相、所依相、所行相、作意相、心起相、安住相、自相相、共相相、麁相、靜相、領納相、分別相、俱行相、染污相、不染污相、正方便相、邪方便相、光明相、觀察相、賢善定相、止相、舉相、觀相、捨相、入定相、住定相、出定相、增相、減相、方便相、引發相。
items.en: There are furthermore thirty-two marks: the mark of one's own mind, the outer mark, the mark of the support, the mark of the [mind's] range, the mark of attention, the mark of the mind's arising, the mark of abiding, the self-mark, the common mark, the coarse mark, the calm mark, the mark of receiving, the mark of discrimination, the mark of accompaniment, the defiled mark, the undefiled mark, the mark of right method, the mark of wrong method, the mark of luminosity, the mark of investigation, the mark of wholesome concentration, the calming mark, the uplifting mark, the insight mark, the equanimity mark, the mark of entering concentration, the mark of abiding in concentration, the mark of emerging from concentration, the mark of increase, the mark of decrease, the mark of method, and the mark of eliciting.

items.zh: 云何自心相？謂有苾芻、先為煩惱染污心故，便於自心極善取相，如是如是心有染污，或無染污。由此方便，心處沈等；由此方便，不處沈等。言沈等者，謂沈等四，乃至令心礙著之相，或復於彼被染污心。
items.en: What is the mark of one's own mind? A monk, whose mind was earlier defiled by affliction, then takes up the mark of his own mind with the utmost skill: in just such a way the mind is defiled, or in just such a way undefiled; by this means the mind falls into dullness and the rest, and by that means it does not. "Dullness and the rest" means the four — dullness, agitation, scatter, attachment — up through whatever mark impedes and snags the mind, or a mind already defiled by them.

items.title: Marks 2–7: The Outer Mark, the Support, the Range, Attention, the Mind's Arising, and Abiding

items.zh: 云何外相？謂即於彼被染污心，了知自心被染污已，便取外相。謂光明相，或淨妙相，或復餘相。為欲除遣諸煩惱故，或令彼惑不現行故。云何所依相？謂分別體相。即是一切自身所攝五蘊并種子相。云何所行相？謂所思惟彼彼境界色乃至法分別體相。
items.en: What is the outer mark? When the mind has been defiled, having recognised that one's own mind is defiled, one takes up an outer mark — a mark of luminosity, or a pure-sublime mark, or some other mark — in order to dispel the afflictions, or to keep them from manifesting. What is the mark of the support? The discriminated substance-mark: namely the mark of all the five aggregates and their seeds included in one's own person. What is the mark of the range? The discriminated substance-mark of the various objects thought upon, from form through mind-objects.

items.zh: 云何作意相？謂有能生作意故，於彼彼境界所生識生，作是思惟：今我此心由作意故，於境界轉，非無作意。此所思惟名作意相。云何心起相？謂即次前所說，是一相。第二相者，謂心緣行、緣名色相。此所思惟名心起相。云何安住相？謂四識住。即識隨色住等。如經廣說。此所思惟，名安住相。
items.en: What is the mark of attention? Because there is an attention able to generate [cognition], the cognition born at each object arises; and one reflects: "now this mind of mine, by reason of attention, turns towards the object — it is not without attention." This reflection is the mark of attention. What is the mark of the mind's arising? The first is just what was said above [attention]; the second is the mark of the mind conditioned by formations, and of the mind and name-and-form conditioning each other. This reflection is the mark of the mind's arising. What is the mark of abiding? The four stations of consciousness — consciousness abiding in dependence on form, and so on, as the scriptures explain at length. This reflection is the mark of abiding.

blocks.text: Having described attention, the treatise turns to the **object** of meditation, which it analyses by four marks. It then describes four obstacles to concentration and begins a list of thirty-two marks a meditator works with. This is the practical heart of the stage: what to attend to, what to avoid, and how to adjust.

subs.head: How each attention conditions the next

blocks.text: The treatise completes its mapping of the seven root attentions onto the forty and shows how each attention conditions the next: the sequence is causal, not just a list.
The object of meditation has four marks:

items: the **object-mark** (所緣相): the image or theme one holds in mind;
the **causal mark** (因緣相): the conditions that support concentration;
the **mark to be avoided** (應遠離相): what disturbs it;
the **mark to be cultivated** (應修習相): what strengthens it.

blocks.text: The marks to be avoided are four:

items: **dullness** (沈沒), which tends to arise in people of deluded temperament;
**agitation** (掉舉), in people of greedy temperament;
**scattering** (散亂), in people of discursive temperament, "fond of wild thinking", as Master Cháng Bǎi puts it;
**attachment** (愛味), relishing the pleasure of concentration itself.

blocks.text: The treatise describes what causes each and what to cultivate against it. Dullness is countered by bright, uplifting objects; agitation by calming ones; scattering by returning to the single object; attachment by seeing the fault even in meditative pleasure (Day 79's "stilled of joy").

Matching remedies to temperament is a hallmark of this treatise. The *Śrāvakabhūmi* develops it into the "purifying objects" for each type: impurity for the greedy, loving-kindness for the angry, dependent origination for the deluded, the breath for the discursive.

The marks to be cultivated are listed as thirty-two. The first is **reading one's own mind** (了別相): knowing at each moment whether the mind is dull, agitated, scattered, or settled. Everything else depends on this.

The next marks include the **outer mark**: "the luminous mark" or "the pure-sublime mark". Master Cháng Bǎi: the luminous mark counters dullness with light; the pure-sublime mark is recollecting the Three Jewels, as in visualising the Buddha's radiant form. Then the support, the range, attention, the mind's arising, and its abiding.
The list reads like an instrument panel. Its point is that concentration is not achieved by force but by continual, fine adjustment, which requires first seeing clearly what the mind is doing.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the four marks of the meditative object?
options: the object-mark, the causal mark, the mark to be avoided, the mark to be cultivated
quiz.why: "First, the object-mark; second, the causal mark; third, the mark to be avoided; fourth, the mark to be cultivated." The causal mark is the provisions for concentration; the marks to avoid are dullness, agitation, scatter, attachment. Master Cháng Bǎi gives a verse listing the provisions.

quiz.q: The text links dullness to the deluded temperament, agitation to the greedy, scatter to the discursive. How does Master Cháng Bǎi sum it up?
options: the deluded tend to dullness, the greedy to agitation, the discursive to scattered thinking
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Those of deluded temperament easily fall into dullness; the greedy become agitated; the discursive, fond of wild thinking, become scattered." He adds: browsing a department store, the mind goes out through the eyes and grows tired.

quiz.q: The "outer mark" takes up a luminous or pure-sublime mark. The note says the pure-sublime counters craving. What do the teachers say these counter?
options: dullness — the pure-sublime mark means recollecting the Three Jewels, visualising the Buddha's radiant marks
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The outer mark is the luminous mark — when dull, counter it with light; or the pure-sublime mark, recollecting the Three Jewels, which also counters dullness." Venerable Miào Jìng: recollection here is mainly visualising the Buddha's radiant marks. The note's "counter craving" is wrong (logged).

quiz.q: Attention on a non-discriminated image cultivates calm. Is it truly without discrimination, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: there is still discrimination, but repeatedly on the same object rather than varied — like counting breaths
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "This 'non-discrimination' still discriminates — just repeatedly on one object rather than on different ones, like counting only the breath." Venerable Miào Jìng: the skeleton appearing in the mind is a "discriminated image."

quiz.q: The attention at "the limit of the thing" knows the bounds of body, feeling, mind, and phenomena. What are the bounds of mind and phenomena, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: mind is the eight consciousnesses, phenomena the 51 or 53 mental factors — beyond these there are none
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Mind is the eight mind-kings; phenomena the 51 or 53 mental factors; beyond these there's no further body, feeling, mind, or phenomenon." The text: one knows "the outer bound of all objects … beyond which there is no further body, feeling, mind, or phenomenon."

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe practising the attention of investigation?
options: in meditation, deliberately calling up some object of desire to see how the mind reacts
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "In meditation, deliberately make some object of desire appear in the mind and see how the mind reacts." Venerable Miào Jìng: a teacher, a companion, or even Māra may test you. This matches §36's sharp-seer calling desires to mind.
